decisions.rationale: Retained 2017 Dresser results explicitly report three DFc1 localities about 2 km apart with microlaminated siliceous rocks interpreted as geyserite. The label and statement preserve attribution and geological setting. Claim kind, earth domain, site scope and placement as an independent node are justified; reported, undated and frontier=false carry only their neutral policy meanings. No edge or directional dependency is asserted.
decisions.limitations: Geological identification is the authors' inference; the captured source alone does not establish independent replication, biological origin or current consensus.

decisions.rationale: At locality 1S the paper describes a 3 cm siliceous unit above stratiform geyserite, with approximately 1 cm convex ridges less than 2 cm high, and says they resemble mid- to distal-apron sinter terracettes. The label, conditional interpretation, earth-domain claim classification, site placement and neutral metadata are faithful. No graph relation is introduced.
decisions.limitations: Resemblance to modern sinters is interpretive; the ridges' construction by microbes is not demonstrated by this specific finding.

decisions.rationale: The paper explicitly proposes that at least some barite masses at upper hydrothermal vein tips are mineralized remnants of terrestrial hot-spring pools with shallow plumbing. The quantifier 'at least some' and proposed status are preserved. Claim identity, earth domain, local geological scope, standalone placement and neutral metadata are supported; no edge direction is claimed.
decisions.limitations: Subsurface-pool reconstruction is proposed from geological geometry; the paper does not extend it to every Dresser barite mass.

decisions.rationale: The source describes numerous approximately 200 µm circular/subcircular structures at locality 16N, interprets them as bubbles, and says entrapment in microbial EPS likely preserved them regardless of thermal-fluid versus metabolic gas source. The statement, claim label, earth domain, site identity and neutral metadata keep these qualifications. No independent graph dependency is inserted.
decisions.limitations: Bubble identity and microbial-EPS trapping remain interpretations; the bubbles' actual gas provenance is unresolved.

decisions.rationale: The retained Dresser article reports vertically aligned, approximately 230 µm quartz crystals in some terracette laminae, suggesting analogy to recrystallized microbial palisade fabric from bedding-perpendicular silicified filaments. The candidate retains 'suggest' and 'analogous', with justified earth-domain claim identity, standalone placement and neutral metadata.
decisions.limitations: Quartz-fabric resemblance does not establish preserved cells, filament taxonomy or unique biogenicity.

decisions.rationale: The source places inferred geyserite rip-up clasts interbedded with domical and conical stromatolitic laminates at locality 24S and says tuffaceous sediment onlap plus internal microfabrics are consistent with microbial origin. The candidate retains the locality and nonexclusive interpretation. Claim kind, earth domain, site placement and neutral metadata are justified, with no graph direction asserted.
decisions.limitations: Consistency with microbial origin is not proof of exclusive microbial genesis; the geyserite-clast identification is itself interpretive.

decisions.rationale: The 2018 paper describes a sampled suite of spheroidal-to-lenticular Dresser structures resembling some previously described Archean microfossils; correlative microscopy of size, walls and chemistry supports the authors' interpretation as silicified and pyritized vesicular volcanic glass. The claim is correctly limited to this suite, placed in earth science, and source-attributed with neutral metadata.
decisions.limitations: The study's abiogenic assessment applies only to the examined microstructures; it does not overturn all Dresser or Archean microfossil reports.

decisions.rationale: The 2018 Dresser source explicitly reports kerogenous material associated with much altered volcanic glass, carbon lining/filling some vesicles, and organic-rich laminae enclosing multiple vesicles. These are associations, represented as such. The claim label, earth-domain scope, sampled-material identity and standalone placement match the retained article and neutral policy.
decisions.limitations: Associated kerogenous carbon does not by itself establish whether vesicles, laminae or carbon are biological.

decisions.rationale: The article warns that reworked, isolated silicified microstructures of the studied volcanic-glass type can adsorb carbon and become pyritized, confusing life-detection interpretation; in those cases nanoscale wall analysis is required to exclude a biological origin. The candidate weakens 'required' to 'may be required' but does not strengthen it; its scope is explicitly conditional. Earth-domain claim and neutral metadata fit.
decisions.limitations: Methodological warning is conditional for these volcanic-glass-like isolated structures, not a universal nanoscale requirement for every candidate biosignature.

decisions.rationale: The 2018 controlled batch-incubation paper reports B. fungorum growth on HSDP2 basalt and Fe/major-element release exceeding abiotic controls only in nutrient-depleted rock-sample assays. The statement keeps the organism, rock source, comparison and exclusivity limited to these assays. The earth-domain claim, neutral metadata and independent-node placement are justified.
decisions.limitations: Limited to a single bacterium and specified laboratory nutrient conditions; no general field-scale or oceanic release rate is established.

decisions.rationale: The retained 2018 source directly says dissolved major-element concentrations in biotic synthetic-basalt-glass colonization experiments increased with increasing residual stress and Fe(II) content. The candidate represents an association over the tested glasses, not separately isolated causation. Claim classification, earth domain, lab scope, descriptive comparison direction and neutral metadata are faithful.
decisions.limitations: Residual stress and Fe(II) vary across the reported treatments, so individual independent causal contributions cannot be inferred.

decisions.rationale: The source directly contrasts intensely biofilm-covered synthetic basalt glasses with residual stress and high Fe(II) against sparse colonization on unstressed, high-Fe(III) glasses. The statement and label retain both coupled conditions and comparison direction. Earth-domain claim, laboratory scope, independent placement and neutral metadata are justified.
decisions.limitations: Stress and iron oxidation state change together in this comparison; neither is proved the sole driver of biofilm coverage.

decisions.rationale: The authors explicitly interpret microlaminated rocks at three DFc1 localities approximately 2 km apart as geyserite. Exact quotations and offsets match. Claim kind, earth domain, neutral reported status, undated era and frontier=false are justified. No identity, taxonomy or directional relationship is proposed.
decisions.limitations: The interpretation relies on stratigraphic, petrographic and geochemical evidence and comparison with younger geyserite. It does not independently prove biological origin. The source notes a published correction whose effects were not separately assessed.

decisions.rationale: Both retained excerpts exactly support the locality 1S ridge measurements and their interpretation as resembling mid- to distal-apron sinter terracettes. Scope and uncertainty are preserved. Claim/earth and neutral reported, undated and frontier=false metadata are appropriate. No relationship or identity merge is proposed.
decisions.limitations: Morphological resemblance and primary porosity support the proposed interpretation but do not establish direct microbial construction.

decisions.rationale: The retained source expressly proposes that at least some large barite masses represent mineralized terrestrial hot-spring pools and shallow hydrothermal plumbing. The candidate preserves that restriction and geological setting. Kind, domain and neutral metadata are justified without inventing relationships or identities.
decisions.limitations: This is an interpretive reassessment of selected barite masses. It does not establish that all Dresser barite masses formed as hot-spring pools.

decisions.rationale: Exact excerpts establish the approximately 200 µm circular structures and explicitly describe likely preservation in microbial EPS while leaving the source of the gas unresolved. The candidate attributes these interpretations rather than asserting demonstrated microbial gas production. Claim/earth and neutral representation metadata are justified; no relation, identity or placement beyond domain is proposed.
decisions.limitations: Bubble identification and EPS entrapment remain interpretations based on textures and analogues. Thermal-fluid degassing and metabolic gas production are both retained as possibilities.

decisions.rationale: The source describes 230 µm vertically aligned quartz crystals within the sinter-terracette unit and explicitly suggests analogy with recrystallized microbial palisade fabric. The candidate preserves the suggested rather than established classification. Claim/earth, reported, undated and frontier=false are justified. No unverified identity or relation appears.
decisions.limitations: The original biological filaments are inferred from mineral textures and geological context. Recrystallization prevents direct identification from this evidence alone.

decisions.rationale: The retained excerpts identify geyserite rip-up clasts interbedded with domical and conical stromatolitic laminates at locality 24S and describe their internal textures and sediment onlap as consistent with microbial origin. The statement retains this evidentiary limitation. Claim/earth and neutral metadata are appropriate; no unsupported relationship, identity or taxonomy is added.
decisions.limitations: Textures consistent with microbial activity do not uniquely establish biological origin. The finding is localized and cannot automatically classify other Dresser structures.

decisions.rationale: The retained primary source describes the studied spheroidal-to-lenticular microstructure suite and interprets it as silicified and pyritized vesicular volcanic glass using size distribution, wall ultrastructure and chemistry. The candidate accurately attributes this interpretation to the study. Kind, domain and neutral representation metadata are justified without identifying unrelated fossils as the same objects.
decisions.limitations: The abiogenic interpretation concerns the examined Dresser sample suite. It neither disproves every reported Archean microfossil nor automatically invalidates separate Dresser biosignatures.

decisions.rationale: The exact excerpt reports kerogenous material associated with altered volcanic glass, organic carbon lining or filling some vesicles, and organic-rich laminae surrounding multiple vesicles. The candidate preserves the observed association and its limited population. Claim/earth and neutral metadata are justified; no additional identity or classification is proposed.
decisions.limitations: Organic carbon accompanying volcanic structures does not demonstrate that the structures themselves are biological or establish the origin of the associated carbon.

decisions.rationale: The source explicitly warns that reworked isolated silicified structures of the studied type can adsorb carbon and become pyritized, creating difficulties in microfossil identification. It also identifies nanoscale wall analysis as a possible necessary discriminator. The candidate preserves the conditional warning. Claim/earth and neutral representation metadata are justified.
decisions.limitations: The caution concerns microstructures of this type. It cannot be generalized into a finding that all carbon-coated Archean or extraterrestrial fossil candidates are abiotic.

decisions.rationale: The retained study explicitly states that Fe and other major-element release from HSDP2 drill-core basalt exceeded abiotic controls only when the rock-sample assay was nutrient depleted. The candidate retains the single-species laboratory context and limiting condition. Claim/earth, reported, undated and frontier=false are appropriate, with no asserted relationship or identity merge.
decisions.limitations: The experiments used Burkholderia fungorum under controlled laboratory conditions with added glucose and low-salt medium. The result does not establish the same response across natural microbial communities, seawater or all basalt environments.

decisions.rationale: The retained source explicitly reports that dissolved major-element concentrations in biotic synthetic-basalt-glass colonization assays increased with residual stress and Fe(II) content. The candidate treats the finding as a reported laboratory association and preserves its joint-factor limitation. Claim/earth and neutral metadata are justified without additional placement or relations.
decisions.limitations: Residual stress and Fe(II) content are not established here as individually isolated causal mechanisms. The finding does not support a universal microbial dissolution rate or response across all basalt glasses.

decisions.rationale: The retained excerpt directly contrasts intense cellular biofilm coverage on stressed Fe(II)-rich basaltic glasses with sparse colonization on unstressed Fe(III)-rich glasses. Dense versus sparse accurately preserves that comparison. Kind, earth domain, reported status, undated era and frontier=false are justified. No unsupported relationship or identity merge is proposed.
decisions.limitations: The contrasted glasses differ jointly in oxidation state and residual stress, so the result cannot isolate either factor as the sole cause. The conclusion is restricted to the reported laboratory colonization assays.
